senses.gloss: ch.<cite ref="N00340">same</cite> <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 2:2">Targ. Gen. II, 2</cite> <he>ונַח</he>.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 21:10">Targ. II Sam. XXI, 10</cite> <he>לִמְנָח</he>; a. fr.—Part. <cite ref="N00660"><he>נְיָיח</he></cite>, <cite ref="N00644"><he>נְיָח</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Numbers 23:24">Targ. Y. Num. XXIII, 24</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 3:25">Targ. Job III, 25</cite> <he>נְיָיחִית</he> (Ms. <he>נָחִית</he>); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 86a:11">B. Mets. 86ᵃ</cite> <he>נַח זעפא</he> the storm subsided.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 86a:9">Ib.</cite> <he>כי הוה נָיְחָא נפשיה</he> when his soul was at rest (when he was dead).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 86a:8">Ib.</cite> <he>תִּינַח נפשיה וכ׳</he> let me rather die, than be delivered &c.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 86a:11">Ib.</cite> <he>ההוא יומא דנח נפשיה</he> on the day when he died.
<cite ref="Ketubot 104a">Keth. 104ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>נח נפשיה ד־</he>—is dead.
<cite ref="Yoma 20b:6">Yoma 20ᵇ</cite> <he>נִינַח מר</he> leave it alone, sir (be no longer my interpreter).
<cite ref="Shabbat 3a">Sabb. 3ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>גופו מֵינַח נָיֵיח</he> Ms. M. (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) his body had been resting (and he lifted it from the ground in moving).
<cite ref="Shabbat 5b:2">Ib. 5ᵇ</cite> <he>מים מי עבידי דנָיְיחֵי</he> is it possible that water (running down an incline) is at rest at any time?; a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Onkelos Deuteronomy 3:20">Targ. O. Deut. III, 20</cite> <he>דִּינִיחַ</he> (ed. Vien. <he>דִּי יְנִיחַ</he>); Y. <he>דְּיָנִיחַ</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Ezekiel 24:13">Targ. Ezek. XXIV, 13</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Targum of II Chronicles 15:15">Targ. II Chr. XV, 15</cite>; <cite ref="Targum of II Chronicles 20:30">XX, 30</cite> <he>אַנְיָיח</he> (ed. Lag. <cite ref="N00341"><he>אניח</he></cite>; fr. <cite ref="N00660"><he>נְיָיח</he></cite>, v. supra).—
<cite ref="Berakhot 28b:1">Ber. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>לַאֲנוּחֵי דעתיה וכ׳</he> to quiet the mind of &c.—[<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 32">Lev. R. s. 32</cite>, a. e. <he>מדכרין ומניחין</he>, v. preced.]

senses.gloss: to rest, put down; to leave alone.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 32:10">Targ. Ex. XXXII, 10</cite> <cite ref="A02152"><he>אַנַּח</he></cite> (O. ed. Vien. <cite ref="E00673"><he>הַנַּחַ</he></cite>; ed. Berl. <cite ref="A00006"><he>אָ׳</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Judges 6:18">Targ. Jud. VI, 18</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 6a:1">Sabb. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>כי מַנַּח ליה</he> when he sets it down.

<cite ref="Ketubot 47b:7">Keth. 47ᵇ</cite> <he>אֲנוּחֵי נַנְחִינְהוּ</he> he must let them lie (store them); a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="M01758"><he>מַנַּח</he></cite>; f. <he>מַנְּחָא</he>; pl. <he>מַנְּחֵי</he>.
<cite ref="Chullin 46a">Ḥull. 46ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>דמ׳ ביה וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="F00084"><he>וַרְדָּא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 84b:2">Keth. 84ᵇ</cite> <he>דמנחי היכא</he> where were they placed (at the time of death)?; a. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Leviticus 26:35">Targ. Y. Lev. XXVI, 35</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 14b:3">B. Bath. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>דמִתְנַח ליה וכ׳</he> (Rashi <he>דמַנַּח</he>, v. supra) it was placed by the side; a. e.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 45b:10">Kidd. 45ᵇ</cite> <he>אִיתְנוּחֵי אִיתְנָחָא ליה</he> it was agreeable to him.

B. Bath. 129ᵃ אִיתְנָחַת לן חדא Ms. R. (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 60; ed. אנחתת, v. נְחַת) one of thy arguments has been satisfactorily disposed of for us.—Contr. אִינַּח.—תִּינַּח, הָתִינַּח (a dialectical term) this might be right, acceptable, might do well.
<cite ref="Shabbat 5a:1">Sabb. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>הת׳ ברשות היחיד וכ׳</he> this might be acceptable with regard to a covered private ground, but &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 132b">Ib. 132ᵇ</cite> <he>ת׳ גדול וכ׳</he> this may apply to an adult, but &c.; a. fr.
